title: Why Bees Visit City Balconies
author: 苏打阅读编辑部
introZh: 从一排阳台花盆看城市中的传粉者，以及普通人能提供的小帮助。
paragraphs: On a row of apartment balconies in the city, small pots of lavender and rosemary attract bees every morning. There are no large fields nearby, but the balconies form a chain of feeding places. A bee can visit one pot, cross a narrow street, and find another flower on the opposite side.

This simple pattern shows why size is not the only thing that matters for urban wildlife. A single pot may offer little food, but many pots can provide meals throughout the day. Different flowers also bloom at different times, so a varied balcony garden can support visitors for more months of the year.

People who want to help do not need to fill every corner with plants. They can choose several kinds of flowers, avoid harmful sprays, and leave a shallow dish of clean water with stones for safe landing. These actions are small, but together they make the city easier for pollinators to cross.
